πυνθάνομαι.long: I ask, inquire, ascertain by inquiry, understand.
πυνθάνομαι.sd: to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from G2065 (ἐρωτάω), which properly means a request as a favor; and from G154 (αἰτέω), which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from G2212 (ζητέω), which implies a search for something hidden; and from G1189 (δέομαι), which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence)
πυνθάνομαι.der: middle voice prolonged from a primary (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses);
πυνθάνομαι.as:
πυνθάνομαι,
[in LXX for דּרשׁ;]
1.to inquire: c. acc. rei, Jo 4:42, Ac 23:20; seq. quæst. indir., Mt 2:4, Lk 15:2618:36, Ac 10:1821:33; quæst. dir., Ac 4:710:2923:19; seq. παρά, c. gen. pers., Mt 2:4, Jo 4:52.
2.to learn by inquiry: seq. ὅτι, Ac 23:34.†

πῦρ.long: fire; the heat of the sun, lightning; fig: strife, trials; the eternal fire.
πῦρ.as:
πῦρ, gen., πυρός, τό,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for אֵשׁ;]
fire: Mk 9:22, Lk 3:9, Jo 15:6, Ac 2:19, I Co 3:13, Ja 3:5, Re 8:5, al; π. καὶ θεῖον, Lk 17:29; κατακαίειν (ἐν) π., Mt 13:40, Re 17:1618:8; καίεσθαι πυρί, He 12:18, Re 8:821:8; φλὸξ πυρός, Ac 7:30, II Th 1:8, He 1:7, Re 1:142:1819:12; λαμπάδες πυρός, Re 4:5; στῦλοι πυρός, Re 10:1; ἄνθρακες πυρός, Ro 12:20(LXX); γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, Ac 2:3; δοκιμάζειν (πυροῦσθαι) διὰ πυρός, I Pe 1:7, Re 3:18; ὡς διὰ. π. (Lft., Notes, 193), I Co 3:15. Of the fire of hell (cf. Dalman, Words,161): Mk 9:48(LXX); τὸ π. τὸ αἰώνιον, Mt 18:825:41 (cf. IV Mac 12:12); ἄσβεστον, Mk 9:43; πυρὸς αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχειν, Ju 7; γέεννα τοῦ π., Mt 5:2218:9; κάμινος τοῦ π., Mt 13:42, 50; ἡ λίμνη τοῦ π., Re 19:2020:10, 14, 15; πυρὶ τηρεῖσθαι, II Pe 3:7; βασανισθῆναι ἐν π., Re 14:10. Metaph.: βαπτίζειν πυρί, Mt 3:11, Lk 3:16; of the tongue, Ja 3:5; of strife and discord, Lk 12:49; ἐκ π. ἁρπάζειν, Ju 23; πυρὶ ἁλίζεσθαι, Mk 9:49; ζῆλος πυρός, He 10:27; of God, π. καταναλίσκον, He 12:29(LXX).

πύλη.sd: a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively)
πύλη.as:
πύλη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly and very freq. for שַׁעַר sometimes for דֶּלֶת, פֶּתַח;]
a gate: Lk 7:12, Ac 9:2412:1016:13, He 13:12; ἡ Ὡραία Π. τ. ἱεροῦ, Ac 3:10. Metaph., Mt 7:13, 14; πύλαι ᾅδου (Wi 16:13, III Mac 5:51, and cf. κλεῖς ᾅδου, Re 1:18): Mt 16:18.†

πυρέσσω.g: I am sick with a fever
πυρέσσω.long: I am sick with a fever.
πυρέσσω.sd: to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever
πυρέσσω.as:
* πυρέσσω
(< πῦρ),
to be ill of a fever: Mt 8:14, Mk 1:3.†

πυρετός.sd: inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever)
πυρετός.as:
πυρετός, -οῦ, ὁ
(< πῦρ), [in LXX: De 28:22 (קדַּחַת)*;]
a fever: Mt 8:15, Mk 1:31, Lk 4:39, Jo 4:52, Ac 28:8; π. μέγας, a high fever: Lk 4:38 (on the technical phrase here, v. MM, xxii).†

πυρράζω.as:
† πυρράζω
(< πυρρός), [in LXX, πυρρίζω: Le 13:19, 42 ff. 14:37 (אֲדַמְדָּם)*;]
to be fiery red: Mt 16:|[2, 3]|.†

πύργος.as:
πύργος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for מִגְדָּל;]
a tower: Lk 13:4; of a watch-tower in a vineyard (Is 5:2): Mt 21:33, Mk 12:1, and prob., Lk 14:28.†

πυλών.g: a large gate, a gateway, porch
πυλών.long: a large gate; a gateway, porch, vestibule.
πυλών.sd: a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule
πυλών.as:
πυλών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(< πύλη), [in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, שַׁעַר;]
1. the porch or vestibule of a house or palace: Mt 26:71, Lk 16:20, Ac 10:1712:13, 14.
2. The gate-way or gate-tower of a walled town: Ac 14:13, Re 21:12, 13, 15, 21, 2522:14.†

πυγμή.sd: the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing)
πυγμή.der: from a primary (the fist as a weapon);
πυγμή.as:
πυγμή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX: Ex 21:18, Is 58:4 (אֶגְרוֹף)*;]
the fist: πυγμῇ νίψασθαι τ. χεῖρας (T, πυκνά; Vg., Goth., Copt., crebro), to wash the hands with the fist (diligently, R, txt.; up to the elbow, R, mg.; the exact meaning is doubtful; v. Swete, in l.): Mk 7:3.†

πυκνά.sd: clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently
πυκνά.as:
πυκιός, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX: Ez 31:3 A (חֹרֶשׁ), III Mac 1:284:10, IV Mac 12:12*;]
1.close, compact, solid.
2.frequent: I Ti 5:23. Neut. pl., πυκνά, as adv., much, often: Mk 7:3 T (v.s. πυγμή), Lk 5:33. Comparat., πυκνότερον, very often or so much the oftener (v. Bl., § 44, 3n): Ac 24:26.†

πύθων.long: a divining spirit, Python, called after the Pythian serpent said to have guarded the oracle at Delphi and been slain by Apollo.
πύθων.sd: a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying)
πύθων.der: from (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located);
πύθων.as:
* πύθων, -ωνος, ὁ,
1. in cl., Python, a serpent slain by Apollo, who is hence surnamed the Pythian.
2. In Plut. (ii, 414 E), a name given to ventriloquist soothsayers (ἐγγαστρίμυθοι; cf. Le 19:3120:6, 27, I Ki 28:7), and perhaps in this sense πνεῦμα πύθωνα, a python-spirit: Ac 16:16.†

Πύρρος.as:
πυρρός, -ά, -όν
(< πῦρ), [in LXX for אֱדֹם;]
fiery red: Re 6:412:3.†

πυκνός.sd: clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently
πυκνός.as:
πυκιός, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX: Ez 31:3 A (חֹרֶשׁ), III Mac 1:284:10, IV Mac 12:12*;]
1.close, compact, solid.
2.frequent: I Ti 5:23. Neut. pl., πυκνά, as adv., much, often: Mk 7:3 T (v.s. πυγμή), Lk 5:33. Comparat., πυκνότερον, very often or so much the oftener (v. Bl., § 44, 3n): Ac 24:26.†

πυρά.long: a fire, pile of burning fuel.
πυρά.as:
** πυρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< πῦρ), [in LXX: Jth 7:5, Wi 17:6, al.;]
a fire: Ac 28:2, 3.†

πυρόομαι.g: I burn, am purified by fire
πυρόομαι.long: pass: I burn, am set on fire, am inflamed; glow with heat, am purified by fire.
πυρόομαι.sd: to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust)
πυρόομαι.kj: burn, fiery, be on fire, try
πυρόομαι.as:
πυρόω, -ῶ
(< πῦρ), [in LXX chiefly for צרף;]
to set on fire, burn up. In NT always pass.,
1.to be set on fire, to burn: Eph 6:16, II Pe 3:12; ptcp., glowing, Re 1:15. Metaph., of grief or indignation, II Co 11:29; of lust, I Co 7:9.
2. Of metals (cf. Jb 22:25, Ps 11 (12):7, Za 13:9), to be refined or purified by fire: Re 3:18 (and so in RV, Re 1:15, but v. supr.).†

πυκτεύω.sd: to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively)
πυκτεύω.der: from a derivative of the same as G4435 (πυγμή);

πύρωσις.sd: ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test)
πύρωσις.as:
πύρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< πυρόω), [in LXX: Pr 27:21 (כּוּר), Am 4:9 (שִׁדָּפוֹן)*;]
1.a burning: Re 18:9, 18.
2.a refining or trial by fire: metaph., I Pe 4:12.†

πυρρός.as:
πυρρός, -ά, -όν
(< πῦρ), [in LXX for אֱדֹם;]
fiery red: Re 6:412:3.†

πύρινος.as:
πύρινος, -η, -ον,
[in LXX: Ez 28:14, 16 (אֵשׁ), Si 48:9*;]
fiery: Re 9:17.†
